surprises.description: Reported adjusted EPS of $6.16 missed the preview’s $6.42–$6.47 consensus, but excluding the $0.69-per-share non-cash TCA deferral headwind, EPS would have been $6.85—above consensus and the preview’s base-case range. The reported miss was therefore driven by a headwind the preview anticipated, while the underlying result was stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $6.16, which would have been $6.85 excluding a non-cash TCA deferral headwind of $0.69 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $6.42 – $6.47”; the preview also described a realistic unofficial bar of “~$6.20–$6.35” and expected the TCA deferral direction to be “Neutral to negative,” with “a $0.60–0.70/share swing.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in at $4.4 billion, slightly below the preview’s consensus range and base-case range. The gap to the low end was small, but the revenue line was identified as the harder test.
Gross profit was below the preview’s estimated $745–$760 million, at $732 million. The reported 16.6% gross margin accompanied that shortfall.
The adjusted operating margin was 4.9%, below the preview’s estimated 5.1–5.3% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$111 million adjusted net income with a 4.9% adjusted operating margin.”

surprises.description: SG&A was 67.4% of gross profit, above the preview’s roughly 66% base estimate, though not as high as its stated stress level. Management reaffirmed the low-60s target for end-2027 and said the improvement would come roughly half from gross-profit growth and half from cost savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A as a percentage of gross profit reaching the low 60% range by the end of 2027, down from 67.4% all-store (67% same-store) in Q3, driven roughly half by gross profit growth and half by cost savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A % of gross profit (adj.): ~66%”; the preview said “below 65% says it's working ahead of schedule” and “>68% says the cost story is slipping.”

surprises.description: Parts and service gross profit was flat and warranty gross profit fell 1%, weaker than the preview’s expectation for low-to-mid-single-digit parts and service growth. Repair orders were down 1.9%; management attributed the weakness largely to Tekion transition disruption rather than consumer weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer pay parts and service gross profit was flat and warranty gross profit was down 1%, with repair order count down 1.9%, attributed largely to Tekion transition disruption rather than consumer weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Parts & service revenue growth” of “+3 to 5%” and said management guided “low-to-mid single digits from Q3 forward.”

surprises.description: Used retail PVR was $1,777, well below the preview’s roughly $1,950 estimate, even as used retail volume improved sequentially. That is a larger margin give-back than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Used retail gross profit grew 3% and used retail PVR rose 10% to $1,777, with all-store used retail volume up 4.5% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated used retail units and GPU at “~34,000 / ~$1,950” and said the base case expected “GPU to give back some ground as the trade-off.”

surprises.description: Same-store new units fell 8%, with EV sales down 76% and accounting for five percentage points of the decline. The preview anticipated EV softness, but did not indicate a company EV sales drop of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store new units fell 8% year-over-year against a tough comparison, with declining EV volume accounting for 5 of the 8 percentage points, as EV sales dropped 76% and represented just 2.1% of total units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said industry Q3 new units were “roughly flat (‑0.5%, ~16.1M SAAR)” and flagged EV softness, noting BEV sales were down 29.2% year-to-date through September.

surprises.description: The company said it would prioritize reducing net leverage to 3.0x before pursuing share buybacks or tuck-in acquisitions. That is a more cautious near-term capital-return stance than the preview’s expected buyback pace, and leverage was 3.5x versus its roughly 3.3x estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at 3.5x with a priority of reaching the 3x target by mid-2027 before pursuing share buybacks and tuck-in acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~3.3x / $100–140M” for leverage and buybacks and said management had indicated that “buybacks beat M&A.”

surprises.description: The FTC administrative proceeding against Asbury was dismissed in early October, a favorable legal development not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FTC administrative proceeding against the company was dismissed in early October.”

surprises.description: The longest-tenured Tekion stores already showed stronger customer-pay gross profit and productivity measures, rather than benefits being deferred entirely to 2027 as the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Longest-tenured Tekion stores (Koons and Georgia) showed customer pay gross profit up 7% versus flat for the total company, with units per salesperson up 4% and gross profit per technician up 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said Tekion benefits would “begin to materialize in 2027”; it described Q3 benefits as deferred to 2027.
